frame_contract_confirmed.worked_example: a5120200000201fa92fd60fa98fe1100ff45 -> mask 0x00000201 (bits 0 and 9), axes fa92fd60fa98fe11, LT 0x00, RT 0xff, checksum 0x45 = sum8 of the preceding 17 bytes

verdict.historical_field_map: CORRECT - PROVEN LIVE. byte15 is LT and byte16 is RT, confirmed against raw frames whose checksum validates.
verdict.analogue_evidence: byte16 reaches 0xff (255) in W1 and takes intermediate values, so the D2 payload's +0x0c/+0x0d carry ANALOGUE values in the live streaming path.
verdict.reconciliation_with_static: Under the dominance result (r13 copy precedes the compare gate and both builders), the packed-bit seed arm would overwrite +0x0d with 0/1 whenever it is taken. The live frames show 0..255, therefore the seed arm is NOT taken on the normal streaming path: the live bytes come from the state+0x1d4 record copy at 0x1e0cd2e. The two are mode-dependent mechanisms, not a precedence chain that always runs.
verdict.no_self_trigger: RT-only movement emits no D2 frame because the D2 emission is gated on a change in the first 14 candidate bytes as compared against the last-sent mirror; the live evidence shows RT state is only observable when another (digital) event drives a frame. The precise reason byte +0x0d does not by itself trip the gate on an RT-only move remains OPEN - the static path says a change there should trip it.
